title: DICT: povi and voli are missing from the dictionary
description: The corpus's 2nd and 8th commonest verbs are absent. entries.jsonl has 'pova (adj) be able, can' and 'vola (adj) wish, will', both Fundamento/UV-1905, both with plainly verbal glosses filed under an adjective ending — the UV cites the ROOT (pov', vol') and the importer appended -a. Independently, DICT/verdicts.jsonl carries {lemma: povi, verdict: inflection, note: 'regular participle of povi'}, a reviewer marking the word an inflection of itself, so mining never promoted it either. Two separate failures on the same two words. Corpus evidence: povas 10825, povis 5018, volas 4944, povus 3489, volis 2138, povos 2103 — 32310 finite tokens between the two lemmas. Found by tools/verb_frequency.py, whose dictionary gate rejected them.
design: pova and vola are also real Esperanto adjectives, so the question is whether to re-cite the UV entries as povi/voli (pos verb, keeping gloss and source) or to add verb entries alongside. The UV glosses are verbal, which argues for re-citing. Non-mined entries survive promote_lemmas.py --rebuild, which only drops source == corpus-mined, so a correction to a Fundamento/UV-1905 entry is durable. The stale verdict must be corrected too or the next mining round re-suppresses the lemma.
acceptance_criteria: povi and voli are listed with pos verb; tools/verb_frequency.py --audit no longer shows them in the root-listed tier; the povi verdict in DICT/verdicts.jsonl is corrected; a mining round does not re-suppress them.
close_reason: tools/repair_uv_verbs.py added povi, voli and eight more Fundamento verb roots, derived from the UV's non-English gloss columns and calibrated against the 901 roots already correct. Stale verdicts reported, not rewritten. Downstream docs re-derived.

title: ANALYSIS: diachronic study of Esperanto 1887-2020s from the corpus
description: Use the corpus as evidence for how Esperanto itself changed: ĥ->k (anarĥio/anarkio, and 651 variant pairs were just recovered from ReVo), -ujo->-io for country names (GRAMMAR 6.1 already records that -ujo dominates, without asking when), internationalisms entering after the Fundamento, and participle and compound-tense usage (GRAMMAR 6.3 records compound tenses are rarer than expected).
design:
Two prerequisites before any measurement.

DATING. The corpus records EDITION dates; language change needs COMPOSITION dates. They diverge by up to 60 years and not randomly — the divergence is concentrated in posthumous collected works, which are among the largest sources. El verkoj de E. Lanti is filed 1982 but collects texts from 1922; Lanti died in 1947. An in-text 'earliest plausible year' heuristic was tested against the 30 independently dated sources and got 11 of 23 wrong, several by 30-60 years, so it is not usable on its own. Build RAW/DATES.tsv with separate written/edition columns, a basis and a confidence, combining curated bibliography, Wikidata P577, filename year and in-text corroboration — and leave 'written' blank where the evidence conflicts rather than picking.

CONFOUNDS. Author, genre and translation status must be recorded per source and controlled for, or the analysis measures Zamenhof-versus-everyone and grammar-versus-novel and calls it time. Translations are the worst case: the Esperanto is of its translator's era while the subject matter is the original's.
acceptance_criteria: Every reported trend states its token coverage, its per-period token counts, and what happens to it when the dominant author or genre of a period is held out.
close_reason: ANALYSIS/diachronic.md delivered: one positive finding (-ujo->-io first attested 1911, p=0.0005 categorical / rho=-0.57 p=0.003 by author), two nulls, and a control that sets a floor. Follow-ups filed as separate beads.

title: DICT: 1471 ReVo headwords are comma-joined variant pairs, not words
description: 5.4% of entries.jsonl has a headword that is not an Esperanto word. The ReVo merge encoded a variant pair as the full first form, a comma, and the distinctive tail of the second: adultulo,ulino for adultulo/adultulino; abrikotujo,arbo for abrikotujo/abrikotarbo; aerarmeo,flugo for aerarmeo/aerflugo; aĥ, with an empty second variant. Two more are multi-word names run together: internaciauniodeteoriakajaplikakemio, paralelaprojekcioparalelopiv1. Consequence: those headwords cannot be looked up, and because load_vocabulary now contributes every headword's stem as a root, they also inject 1471 junk roots into the morphology, where they can make a damaged or foreign word analyse as known.
acceptance_criteria: Every headword in entries.jsonl is a single word: no commas, no whitespace. The second variant is recovered as its own entry where it can be reconstructed and checked, and recorded rather than discarded where it cannot.
notes: Correction to the description above: the claim that these inject 1471 junk roots into the morphology is wrong. load_vocabulary derives a stem with strip_ending, which on 'abrikotujo,arbo' yields 'abrikotujo,arb' — a string containing a comma, which the tokenizer can never produce, so it is inert rather than harmful. The entries' own 'root' fields are clean ('aboli,i' has root 'abol'). The real cost is the one that remains: 1466 headwords that cannot be looked up.
close_reason: Fixed by tools/repair_headwords.py: 1466 comma-joined headwords truncated at the comma with the original string kept in revo_raw, 13 with a bibliographic reference glued on dropped and listed, 205 duplicates that truncation exposed collapsed keeping the better-sourced entry, 5 glosses stripped of a leaked ReVo officialness marker. Every headword in entries.jsonl is now a single word: 0 with a comma, 0 with a space. The second variant is NOT reconstructed — see esp-1u4 for why and for what a re-merge needs to do.

title: Mining: min-count was applied per shard, discarding globally-attested words
description: The map applied --min-count 2 to each shard's own tally, but the corpus is split by file, so a word attested once in each of four books reached 2 in no shard and was discarded before the reduce ever saw it. Found by tracing 112 approved lemma verdicts that had lost their record: duondorme (4 occurrences across 4 books), eŭkaristio (2 across 2), enrigardado (3 across 3), dusence (4 across 4).
design: The map now keeps everything (--min-count 1) and the reduce applies the threshold after summing, skipping any lemma a reviewer has already judged. 61368 true singletons are dropped at the reduce; 8 of the 9 traced words are back.
close_reason: Fixed: the threshold moved from the map to the reduce, where the counts from all shards are summed. Also fixed the related keying defect that exposed it — shard records were keyed by the analysed root ('banlok'), which is not a word and not what any reviewer had seen, so improving the morphology moved the key and orphaned 917 approved lemmas. Records are now keyed by the word's own citation form. The lost verdicts were recovered by merging the committed ledger with the 211 raw reviewer batch files: 8091 verdicts, 5218 of them 'lemma'.

title: Re-extract the wsdump sources: the template resolver dropped text
description: tools/fetch_raw_vikifontaro.py resolve_template filtered every argument matching FORMAT_ARG before choosing which one carried the text, and FORMAT_ARG matches the single letters c, l, r, j and m as alignment codes. eo.wikisource writes {{SIC|c|C}}ezaro where the book prints a lowercase initial — 132 times in Quo vadis I — and both arguments were filtered away, leaving 'ezaro'. Verified against the dump's own wikitext, not inferred. Separately, {{lang|la|}} with an empty text argument fell back to the language code and published it as a word, which is the source of the 105 'la la' sequences in the same file (7 in volume II).
design: Fixed in resolve_template: the last-argument path no longer filters, so a correction template yields its correction; alignment keywords are dropped only when another argument survives; a single argument is content by necessity ({{sc|C}}); measurements are never content. Measured over all 22214 Paĝo: pages the fix changes 790 resolutions, of which 788 are corrections (175 sic, 4 large initials, 609 stray sizes such as {{gap|3.5em}} that were previously emitted as text) and 2 are stray characters from a template whose text contains a ref tag.
acceptance_criteria: After re-extraction, standalone 'ezaro' is 0 and 'la la' drops to the level of volume II.
close_reason: Fixed and re-extracted. resolve_template no longer filters on the last-argument path, so {{SIC|c|C}}ezaro yields Cezaro; alignment keywords are dropped only when another argument survives; a lone argument is content; measurements never are. Also added the missing {{Lingvo}} alias (552 uses) and fixed the page-break hyphenation pair {{vdk}}/{{vdf}}, which had been returning only the second half of every split word. Standalone 'ezaro' is now 0 (was 113); 'la la' is 3 (was 105, against 7 in volume II); 'demandos' is whole again.

title: citation_form does not reduce participles to the infinitive
description: Participial adjectives, adverbs and nouns are filed as their own headwords: alnajlita, neĝkovrita, mokridante, duonfrenezigite, mirkonsternite, radŝirata, altirata, laŭirante, preterlasinte. The shard 4 reviewer measured 31 of 320 candidates (9.7%) in this class and the shard 6 and 8 reviewers reported the same, all noting the roots are already in DICT/entries.jsonl.
design: Extend citation_form: strip a participle affix (ant|int|ont|at|it|ot) together with its ending and return the infinitive. Must not fire where the participle affix is really part of the root.
close_reason: Added esperanto.participle_infinitive, used by the miner rather than by citation_form. Only the adjectival and adverbial participles are reduced: reducing the nominal ones turned vizito into 'vizi', soldato into 'soldi' and komitato into 'komiti', and no vocabulary check catches that, because sold- is a root and Esperanto really would build 'soldi' from it. Verified on all 18 forms the reviewers cited and on 12 nouns that must be left alone.

title: analyse() checks for compounds before removing the grammatical ending
description: The two-root compound check in analyse() runs over the whole token, so it only fires on a bare stem-plus-nothing form. 'banloko' is known (ban + loko) but 'banlokoj' is unknown: the ending loop tries stem 'banlok' against roots and peel_affixes, neither of which knows about compounding, and the compound loop then tries to match the tail 'lokoj' as a root. The shard 5 reviewer measured 60 of 320 candidates (19%) that analyse() already recognises in some other surface form — batalkampo, sidloko, laborilo and the like.
acceptance_criteria: analyse('banlokoj') and analyse('batalkampojn') return 'known'.
close_reason: The compound test now runs on the stem as well as the whole token, allows the connecting vowel (vent-o-montrilo) and strips the second root's own ending. banlokoj, batalkampojn, sidloko, laborilo and ventomontrilo all resolve. Audited the result: of 7198 lemmas accepted only by this rule, a random sample is almost entirely genuine compounds, but the highest-frequency ones were proper names accepted as compounds (Vinicii as vin+icii, 910 occurrences), so the name rule now overrides the morphology when a lemma appears capitalised more than once and never in lower case.

title: esperanto.py: PREFIX has no prepositional prefixes and SUFFIX lacks -il and -ing
description: PREFIX covers mal/ne/ge/bo/ek/el/re/dis/for/pra/eks/mis/fi/retro but not the prepositional prefixes al-, en-, sur-, tra-, kun-, ĉirkaŭ-, sub-, super-, inter-, kontraŭ-, preter-, trans-. SUFFIX omits -il, one of the most productive suffixes in the language, and -ing. Consequence: alkudri, entenata, surkudrita, sonileto, ventomontrilo, altirata, laŭirante and 30+ other ordinary derivations reach the review queue as unknown vocabulary. Reported by the shard 6 and shard 7 reviewers.
acceptance_criteria: analyse() returns 'known' for alkudri, ventomontrilo, altirata and trapasante without any new dictionary entry.
close_reason: PREFIX gained the 22 prepositional prefixes (al, antaŭ, apud, ĉe, ĉirkaŭ, de, en, inter, kontraŭ, krom, kun, per, post, preter, pri, pro, sen, sub, super, sur, tra, trans) and SUFFIX gained -il and -ing. alkudri, surkudrita, entenata, altirata, trapasante and englutinta all resolve now.

title: esperanto.py: whole-word entries contribute no stem, so their inflections read as unknown
description: load_vocabulary adds entry['word'] to 'words' and entry['root']/morphology.stem to 'roots', but a corpus-promoted entry like 'laŭtlegi' has no root recorded. So analyse('laŭtlegi') is known while analyse('laŭtlegis') is unknown: the stem 'laŭtleg' is in neither set. Proof is in the shard files — the same lemma is kind=unknown in shards 1,2,4,7 and kind=known in shard 6, decided purely by which surface form each shard happened to meet first. Reviewers in rounds 3 and 4 spent 22-34 verdicts per shard on this, and three reported it independently.
design: Derive a stem set in load_vocabulary by stripping one grammatical ending from every whole word longer than 3 characters, and consult it in analyse alongside roots. Re-mine afterwards; verdicts survive via the ledger.
close_reason: load_vocabulary now contributes the stem of every whole word longer than three characters, so an entry promoted from the corpus is recognised in all its inflections. roots grew from about 16k to 22759. laŭtlegis, englutinta and enpaki now analyse as known in every shard rather than in whichever one happened to meet the infinitive first.

title: Mining: filter foreign text per line, not per file
description: Every reviewer in mining round 3 reported the same thing: 185-234 of every 320 unknown candidates were foreign words, not vocabulary gaps. They come from bilingual sources that per-file exclusion cannot reach — the dlibra Esperanto-German periodical, the Ekzercaro's German/French/English translation columns, publisher furniture and quoted passages inside otherwise clean books. Score each LINE for recognisability and skip the foreign ones.
acceptance_criteria: Unknown-candidate count drops substantially; a sample of dropped lines from a clean source contains no Esperanto prose.
close_reason: Implemented as mine_lemmas.line_is_foreign: a recognisability floor per line plus a curated list of foreign function words for lines too short to score. Unknown candidates per shard fell from 1633-2118 to 781-1271 while derived lemmas dropped 2%; the words that disappeared were the(693), of(337), that(90), be(82). Reviewers in the following round reported foreign leakage down to 7-41 of 320, nearly all single words quoted inside Esperanto sentences, which no per-line rule can catch.

title: RAW: decide whether to keep pg-23586, which is copyrighted
description: RAW/PROVENANCE.md recorded pg-23586 (Jorge Camacho, 'La liturgio de l'\'' foiro') as Project Gutenberg public domain, but Gutenberg's own bibrec says 'Copyrighted. Read the copyright notice inside this book for details.' and the file itself carries 'kopirajto (c) ĉe la aŭtoro kaj la eldonejo' (Progresema Esperanto-Forumo, 1999). PG hosts it with the rightsholder's permission; that permission does not obviously extend to redistributing it in this repo, and it is the only non-public-domain text in RAW/ (the other 9 batch-1 Gutenberg ids verify as public domain). The provenance line is now corrected to state the real status. Deciding whether to drop the file, seek permission, or keep it under a documented exception is a licensing call for a human, not an agent.
acceptance_criteria: A human has decided: file removed from RAW/ (and CORPUS regenerated), or an explicit permission/exception is documented in PROVENANCE.md.
close_reason: Skipped per owner decision: quarantined in QUARANTINE/, excluded from the corpus, provenance and rationale recorded.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text: Decided by the repo owner: skip it. pg-23586 moved to QUARANTINE/pg-23586.txt via git mv so the history survives; its RAW/PROVENANCE.md line is struck through with the reason, and QUARANTINE/README.md records the copyright evidence (PG bibrec 'Copyrighted' plus the in-file 'kopirajto (c) ĉe la aŭtoro kaj la eldonejo', Progresema Esperanto-Forumo 1999). tools/normalize_corpus.py reads only RAW/*.txt, so it no longer reaches CORPUS/ — regenerated at 131 sources.

title: GRAMMAR: outline the guide from Unua Libro and Dua Libro
description: wsrc-Unua_Libro.wikitext and pg-20006 (Dua Libro) are the primary sources. Draft GRAMMAR/OUTLINE.md: the 16 rules, the alphabet, affix system, correlative table, and verb/participle system, each mapped to the source passage it comes from.
close_reason: Superseded by landed work: GRAMMAR/grammar.md has the chapter structure (Fundamentoj, Morfologio, Sintakso, Fonologio/Ortografio, Pragmatiko) plus GRAMMAR/index.md (main 50b54a0, PR #3).

title: DICT: define the JSONL entry schema
description: Fix the shape of a DICT/ entry before bulk extraction: headword, POS, morphological decomposition (root + affixes + ending), gloss(es), and citation list pointing at source id + offset. One JSON object per line. Document it in DICT/SCHEMA.md.
close_reason: Superseded by landed work: DICT/README.md documents the JSONL schema (required word/pos/gloss_en; optional gloss_fr/root/morphology/source) and DICT/entries.jsonl ships 2911 conforming entries (main 514ca3e, PR #5).

title: Corpus normalizer for RAW/ sources
description: Turn the RAW/ sources into clean, uniform text the DICT and GRAMMAR passes can consume. Reality after PR #4: RAW/ holds 10 pg-*.txt (Project Gutenberg, still carrying START/END boilerplate, licence blocks and transcriber notes) and 79 wsrc-*.txt from Vikifontaro (wikitext already stripped upstream, but each carries multilingual title/nav headers and footer cruft). Emit one normalized text per source under a directory the later passes read, keyed to the source id in RAW/PROVENANCE.md. Also normalize x-system/h-system spellings to UTF-8 diacritics where they occur.
notes: Implemented as tools/normalize_corpus.py → CORPUS/ (89/89 sources). pg-*: sliced between Gutenberg START/END markers, plus the older unfenced 'End of Project Gutenberg's ...' line, the 'Produced by' credit and one transcriber's note block. wsrc-*: preamble dropped at the run-together metadata line (collection/book/page-number glued to the title) for 77 files; 2 index-like pages use pattern fallback and are flagged 'wsrc-fallback' in the manifest. x-system → UTF-8 diacritics in the 6 files where it is dominant, gated at 100 hits so English words in pg-16967 (auxiliary, flux) are not corrupted. Verified: 0 residual Gutenberg boilerplate, 0 residual x-system in converted files, and every RAW line absent from CORPUS accounted for as furniture, a stripped footnote arrow, or an x-system rewrite. 57709 body lines kept, 5808 furniture lines dropped. Derived text is gitignored; CORPUS/MANIFEST.tsv records per-source method, line counts and output hash.
close_reason: tools/normalize_corpus.py normalizes all 89 RAW/ sources into CORPUS/ with a per-source manifest.

title: ANALYSIS: the 1940-1990 gap cannot be closed by re-dating; fetch sources from that period
description:
esp-e0q raised the dated share 46% -> 64% by bytes and added 21 authors, and moved the count of sources between 1939 and 1990 from three to three. The 41 new dates land 1891-1924 and 1997-2003 because that is the shape of Project Gutenberg's Esperanto holdings: pre-1929 public domain plus modern donated translations.

Post-war Esperanto is where -io is generally said to have won, and the corpus cannot see it. Closing it needs new RAW sources, not better dating of the ones here. Candidates worth a licence check: Sennacieca Revuo and Sennaciulo runs, Heroldo de Esperanto, Norda Prismo, and the 1950s-70s Stafeto books. See ANALYSIS/diachronic.md addendum 2026-09-06.

title: DICT: ingest ReVo transitivity marks as a second, independent basis
description: ReVo hand-marks transitivity in <gra><vspec>tr|ntr</vspec></gra> and merge_revo.py ignores it: 745 marked drv elements in a 970-article sample alone, 473 tr and 213 ntr. The dictionary now carries a corpus-measured transitivity field (665 entries, tools/annotate_transitivity.py); ReVo would supply a second basis for a different question. Where both commit to a verdict they already agree 75 of 76, which is an external validation of the measurement, since the thresholds were never tuned against ReVo.
design: Keep the two bases separate rather than merging them into one verdict. They answer different questions and the single disagreement shows it: vespermangxi is ReVo tr but takes an object in 4% of its 112 corpus clauses, because ReVo records what a verb CAN take and the corpus what writers DO. Suggest transitivity.basis gaining a value of revo alongside corpus, or a parallel field, so a consumer can ask either question. The 25 cases where ReVo commits and the corpus says uncertain are the immediate win: ReVo settles them for free.
acceptance_criteria: Entries carry ReVo transitivity where ReVo marks it, kept distinct from the corpus measurement; the agreement rate between the two is reported and machine-checked; DICT/README documents which field answers which question.

title: DICT: decide whether an untranslated ReVo derivation earns an entry
description: DICT/tools/merge_revo.py drops any ReVo derivation head that has no English translation ('skip_noen'). DICT/README records the count without the consequence: 11793 of 30648 derivation heads, 38%, never entered the dictionary. Measured over 970 cached ReVo articles this is the dominant cause of the gap in ANALYSIS/verbs.md — 220 of the 229 missing -i headwords have no English gloss, against 4 lost to any other cause. ReVo leaves a derivation untranslated precisely BECAUSE it is transparent: reordigi, dolorigxi, ekkompati, foruzi, peligxi, subluigi, fiparoli. These are ordinary Esperanto words the dictionary cannot find.
design: This is a policy decision, not a bug, which is why it is a bead and not a patch. Three options. (1) Keep the rule: a bilingual dictionary needs a gloss, and 11793 glossless entries help nobody. (2) Admit them with a gloss synthesised from the morphology — the project already emits per-morpheme glosses in the "morphology" field of each entry and holds DICT/affix-examples.jsonl, so "reordigi = re- + ord + -ig- + -i" is derivable; the risk is fluency and silent wrong compositions. (3) Admit them with gloss_en null plus the segmentation, so a reader gets the parts and no invented English. Option 3 is honest and cheap; option 2 is more useful and needs an audit of what it generates. Whichever is chosen, a full re-merge needs the complete revo-fonto source, which this session could not obtain: GitHub access is scoped to alexcasper/esperanto, the release tarball is refused, and reaching the same content by another route would be circumventing that denial rather than respecting it.
acceptance_criteria: A decision is recorded in DICT/README.md with its reasoning; if entries are admitted, merge_revo.py implements it and the count of admitted-vs-skipped heads is reported and machine-checked by tools/check_figures.py.
notes:
CRUCIAL CLARIFICATION: these are NOT derivations this project generated. They are hand-written ReVo editorial entries. The dropped drv for "ordi" (root ord) carries: mrk="ord.0i", a grammar tag <gra><vspec>ntr</vspec></gra>, an Esperanto definition "Esti en bona ordo", two cited attestations with full bibliography (N. Nicholas, Balado jarresuma, 2003; MkM chapter 18), and translations into Belarusian, Polish and Romanian. Everything except an English trdgrp. We discard the whole entry for the one column it lacks.

This adds a FOURTH option, better than the three already listed: admit the entry carrying ReVos own Esperanto definition (dif) and grammar marks, with gloss_en absent. No invented English, and strictly more information than the dictionary holds today. Option 3 (null gloss plus segmentation) now looks weak because it discards a definition that is sitting in the source.

SEPARATE FINDING, worth its own work: ReVo hand-marks transitivity. 745 drv elements in the 970-article cache carry <vspec>, 473 tr and 213 ntr. The merge ingests none of them. Checked against the corpus measurement in ANALYSIS/transitivity.md, which was never tuned against ReVo: where both commit to a verdict they agree 75 of 76 (51 tr/transitive, 24 ntr/intransitive, 1 disagreement), plus 25 where the corpus says uncertain. That is an independent external validation of the measured field. The one disagreement is vespermangxi: ReVo tr, corpus 4% object share over 112 clauses. Not an error either way — ReVo records what the verb CAN take, the corpus what writers DO.

title: DICT: derive a transitivity field from the corpus
description: entries.jsonl records no transitivity, and it is the hardest thing about Esperanto verbs for a learner. tools/transitivity.py measures it over 698315 verb clauses and calibrates cleanly (lowest undisputed transitive 34.0%, highest undisputed intransitive 6.3%). The -ig-/-igx- result — 17 pairs, mean gap 72.1 points, none reversed — shows the signal is real. This would be the first dictionary field derived from measured syntax rather than a source's assertion.
design: Do not promote the ratio. Promote a verdict with the evidence behind it: transitive above ~60% over 400+ clauses, intransitive below ~5%, and the band between goes to a reviewer, which is where the genuinely ambitransitive verbs live. The floor is 6% and is the bare directional accusative (iri Parizon), so nothing below that separation means anything. Entries should carry the clause count like a mined lemma carries its frequency.
acceptance_criteria: Verbs in entries.jsonl carry a transitivity field with clause counts; the uncertain band is reviewed rather than guessed; GRAMMAR §6.6 links to it.
close_reason: 662 verb entries carry measured transitivity (366/155/141). Thresholds set inside the calibration gap so nothing as hard as the hardest known case is auto-decided; validated on 107 -ig-/-iĝ- verbs with zero contradictions. Field, limits and pipeline order documented.

title: ANALYSIS: measure verb transitivity from the corpus
description: Transitivity is the hardest thing about Esperanto verbs for a learner — komenci vs komencigxi, sxangxi vs sxangxigxi — and DICT/entries.jsonl records no transitivity at all. PIV marks verbs tr./ntr. by lexicographic assertion; the corpus can measure it. The -ig-/-igx- pair is the transitivity machinery and leads every other affix by verb tokens (8557 and 6739), so the data is there.
design: For each verb occurrence, look for an accusative noun phrase in the same clause. Three confounds will produce garbage if not handled, and all three are why this needs an audit rather than a count: (1) the DIRECTIONAL accusative — 'iri Parizon', 'en la domon' — marks motion, not an object, and would make iri look transitive; (2) the ADVERBIAL accusative of time and measure — 'la tutan tagon', 'tri fojojn' — is not an object either; (3) free word order means the object may precede the verb, so a forward-only window undercounts. Calibrate against verbs whose transitivity is not in doubt: vidi, havi, fari, doni, preni must score high and esti, iri, veni, resti, sidi, stari, morti, okazi must score low. If the calibration set does not separate, the measure is wrong and no other number from it means anything.
acceptance_criteria: tools/transitivity.py reports a transitivity ratio per verb with the clause counts behind it; the calibration set separates cleanly; an --audit mode shows what is being counted as an object; ANALYSIS/ records the findings including the -ig-/-igx- pairs and any disagreement with received transitivity.
close_reason: ANALYSIS/transitivity.md and tools/transitivity.py delivered; GRAMMAR §6.6 records the -ig-/-iĝ- result. Calibration separates 34.0% vs 6.3%; 17 pairs, mean gap 72.1 points, none reversed. Also corrected the diachronic accusative control it exposed.

title: GRAMMAR and DICT: audit the derived figures that drift as the data grows
description: Three figures in GRAMMAR §6 were stale by large factors, found while writing the verb findings in: Francujo 172/Francio 1 was really 299/85; Anglujo 95/Anglio 4 was really 240/26; negative correlatives 5965 lines was really 13761; ne-plus-neni- 10 lines was really 58. All four predate corpus growth and the find_examples exclusion-list fix, and were never rechecked. The ones checked so far were checked because the verb work happened to touch them, which is not an audit. Every remaining numeric claim in grammar.md should be re-derived against the current 240-source corpus.
design: tools/check_grammar_citations.py now verifies quotations but says nothing about counts, because a count has no quoted text to match. Either add a machine-checkable form for frequency claims — an inline pattern the tool can re-run, the way citations carry source:line — or re-derive by hand and record the command next to each figure. The first is better: the same drift will happen again the next time the corpus grows.
acceptance_criteria: Every numeric claim in GRAMMAR/grammar.md is reproduced by a printed command over the current corpus, or corrected; the mechanism for keeping them honest is written down.
notes: Extended beyond GRAMMAR after DICT/README.md was found stale by the same mechanism: it says 'Every count in this section was measured against entries.jsonl as it stands, not carried forward from an earlier pass', and its verb count was 4153 against an actual 4159 BEFORE the ten UV verbs were added. Every one of these documents asserts numbers derived from data that changes underneath them, and nothing recomputes or checks them. tools/check_grammar_citations.py verifies quotations but says nothing about counts. The fix is the same for both files: a machine-checkable form for a derived figure, so it fails loudly like a broken citation instead of quietly going stale.
close_reason: tools/check_figures.py annotates derived figures with an inline expression marker and verifies them; 30 annotated across DICT/README.md, GRAMMAR/ and ANALYSIS/ source counts, all passing, exit-non-zero on drift, --fix rewrites. Study results in ANALYSIS/ deliberately dated rather than annotated. Added to the documented gates in CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md.

title: DICT: 918 roots the corpus conjugates that ReVo leaves untranslated
description: tools/verb_frequency.py's root-listed tier is 54023 tokens over 1051 lemmas where the dictionary records a root's -o/-a/-e form but not its verb, while the corpus inflects it. Head of the list: eniri 2628 (has eniro), foriri 2153 (foriro), plenigi 750 (plenigo), aspekti 750 (aspekte), trafi 635 (trafo), klopodi 470 (klopodo), kapabli 459 (kapabla), rajti 426 (rajta), sopiri 417, aliri 441, utili 394, sperti 392, valori 327, deklari 313, temi 304. Fundamento Rule 6 makes every root a verb by adding -i, so the dictionary is not wrong exactly — but a reader looking up 'eniri' finds nothing, and every tool that gates on pos == verb undercounts.
design: Not a code change: deciding which of the 1051 deserve an entry is review judgement, and the tail mixes genuine adjectival verbs (belas, novas, afablas are real Esperanto) with residual noise. Suggest a mining-style round over the root-listed list ranked by corpus frequency, with a floor — the top ~200 by token count are almost all uncontroversial. tools/verb_frequency.py --audit prints the list with the dictionary's existing citation for each.
acceptance_criteria: The root-listed tier shrinks materially; each promoted verb carries corpus frequency and citations like any mined lemma; the residual tail is documented rather than silently included.
notes: Also visible from the transitivity work: plenigi is not a dictionary entry at all, though the corpus gives it 541 verb clauses and it is one of the clearest -ig- transitives measured (83%). Of 17 -ig-/-iĝ- pairs measurable in the corpus, only 12 have both halves present in entries.jsonl. The gap costs the dictionary derived forms as well as root verbs.
close_reason: Diagnosed and largely explained rather than reviewed. Of the missing ReVo -i headwords in a 970-article sample, 220 of 229 have no English gloss and were dropped by merge_revo.py's documented skip_noen rule — a policy question now filed as esp-spg. 118 more are the whitespace-squash defect, filed as esp-lwj. Only 4 were genuinely restorable and are restored: fiksi, forlasi, rediri, sanigi, three of them rejected during mining as an inflection of themselves. tools/restore_revo_gaps.py reproduces the whole accounting.

title: ANALYSIS: verb prevalence in the corpus
description: Which verbs the corpus actually uses, how concentrated the distribution is, and whether the ranking is a property of Esperanto or of whoever wrote the text. Esperanto's design claim is that a small root inventory plus productive affixes covers the language; a verb frequency list is a direct test of that, since -ig-/-igx-/mal-/ek-/re- derivations should carry a measurable share of verb tokens. Also: tense and mood distribution per verb, which grammars assert and no one has measured here.
design: Lemmatise with tools/esperanto.py citation_form (already maps finite and imperative forms to the infinitive) plus participle_infinitive. Hazards: -i and -u are not reliable verb markers (mi/vi/li/gxi/ni/si/tri, kiu/tiu/iu/cxiu/neniu, unu all end that way), so GRAMMATICAL and CORRELATIVE must be excluded; nominal participles -ato/-ito are the shape of Latinate nouns (vizito, soldato, komitato) and must not be reduced. Validate every lemma against DICT/entries.jsonl rather than trusting the ending. Stability checked with the author-pooling machinery from ANALYSIS/diachronic.md, not by decade.
acceptance_criteria: tools/verb_frequency.py runs over CORPUS/ and reports a ranked lemma list with tense/mood breakdown and derived-vs-simple share; ANALYSIS/verbs.md records the findings with the false-positive audit; every quantitative claim reproducible from a printed command.
close_reason: ANALYSIS/verbs.md and tools/verb_frequency.py delivered. Follow-up dictionary defects filed as esp-* beads.

title: CORPUS: fill 1940-1990, where -io actually won
description:
Post-war Esperanto is where -io is generally said to have won, and the corpus cannot see it.

Three dated sources sit between 1939 and 1990, and only two are usable: Rossetti 1950 (high) and Omelka 1952 (medium). The third is the Downes textbook dated 1982, which is English prose about Esperanto and sits on the mining exclusion list, so no analysis reads it. The 1940s, 1960s and 1970s contain nothing at all. Decade coverage after esp-e0q: 1880s=3 1890s=5 1900s=43 1910s=19 1920s=25 1930s=5 1950s=2 1980s=1 1990s=14 2000s=3 2020s=1.

ANALYSIS/diachronic.md can see -ujo -> -io begin in 1911 and cannot see it complete. That is the one positive finding in the study and it is missing its second half.

ESTABLISHED EMPIRICALLY (was esp-rph, merged here): this gap cannot be closed by better dating of what is already in RAW/. esp-e0q resolved 34 translators against Wikidata and raised the dated share 46% -> 64% by bytes, adding 41 sources and 21 independent authors — and moved the 1939-1990 count from three to three. The 41 new dates land 1891-1924 and 1997-2003, because that is the shape of Project Gutenberg holdings: pre-1929 public domain plus modern translations donated by their translators. Nothing between. Closing this needs new RAW sources, full stop.
design:
Candidates worth a licence check, from the esp-rph investigation: Sennacieca Revuo and Sennaciulo runs (SAT, and Lanti-adjacent, so directly relevant to the -io question); Heroldo de Esperanto; Norda Prismo; the 1950s-70s Stafeto books. Periodicals are the better target than books for two reasons: they carry many hands per volume, which is what the author hold-out needs and what the corpus is short of after 1939, and they are movement prose, which is where -io appeared first.

Licence is the binding constraint, not availability. Most of this period is still in copyright. Check what SAT and UEA have released, and what is on Vikifontaro under a free licence, before fetching anything. RAW/PROVENANCE.md records a licence basis per source and that has to be honest.

Beware the register confound while doing it (esp-yvm): the texts that use -io earliest are disproportionately movement and reference prose, so filling the gap with periodicals alone would confound period with register in exactly the way author was confounded with period before.
acceptance_criteria: At least three independent authors per decade for 1940-1990 in RAW/, dated at medium confidence or better, with an honest licence basis recorded in RAW/PROVENANCE.md for each. tools/diachronic.py --by-author gains authors in those decades, and the -ujo/-io question can be asked of the period the change is said to have completed in.

title: ANALYSIS: date the 76 translator-named sources via translator identity
description: 76 sources name a translator and are undated because the in-text year dates the original work, not the Esperanto. Translator identity dates them, and Wikidata covers people far better than it covers obscure Esperanto translations: Edwin Grobe (1927-2015) and H. J. Bulthuis (1865-1945) both resolve where their books do not. Highest-yield way to raise dated coverage above 46% of the corpus by bytes.
acceptance_criteria: RAW/DATES.tsv dated share rises materially above 46%; each new date records translator-lifespan as its basis; tools/diachronic.py --by-author gains authors in the 1940-1990 gap.
close_reason: 41 sources newly dated at medium via translator working-life windows from Wikidata; dated share 46% -> 64% by bytes, --by-author 38 -> 59 authors. Follow-ups: esp-kb0 (14 unresolved names), esp-fez (PG Edition line in CORPUS), esp-rph (1940-1990 gap needs new sources, not re-dating).

title: DICT: six correlatives were missing from a closed 45-word grid
description: The tabelvortoj are a closed class of exactly 45 words, nine endings by five series, complete by rule. The dictionary held 39. Missing: nenial, neniom, ties, ĉial, ĉies, ĉiom — not rare or doubtful words, just cells nobody sourced. A reader who looks up kial and tial and then fails to find ĉial is being told something false about the language. Found while cross-linking entries to GRAMMAR sections, which is what surfaced the count.
design: tools/complete_correlatives.py generates the missing cells from the grid rather than transcribing them, so the glosses cannot drift from GRAMMAR/grammar.md, which carries the same table with corpus citations. Tagged source: correlative-grid, so the provenance is honest — these are generated from a rule, not attested.
close_reason: All 45 cells present. tools/complete_correlatives.py generated the six missing ones from the grid — nenial, neniom, ties, ĉial, ĉies, ĉiom — tagged source: correlative-grid so the provenance stays honest about being generated rather than attested.

title: Mining: line-end hyphens are not rejoined
description: A word broken across a line by a typesetter's hyphen is mined as two candidates. Reviewers named 'taĝo' from 'avan- taĝojn', 'tanta' from 'konsis-tanta' and 'ĝas' from 'lo-ĝas' in the wsdump Quo vadis. This is distinct from the page-break case, which eo.wikisource marks with {{vdk}}/{{vdf}} and which is already fixed: here the hyphen is inside the page and carries no markup, so it has to be detected in normalize_corpus by the shape — a hyphen at end of line followed by a lowercase continuation whose join is a word the dictionary recognises.
close_reason: normalize_corpus.rejoin_hyphens joins a word the typesetter broke across a line, but only where the join is a word the dictionary knows: 480 of the corpus's 724 such breaks qualified at the time of measurement, 675 breaks across 28 files were joined in the current build. The rest stay as found, because a line-end hyphen is also how a genuine compound falls (Nordrejn-Vestfalio) and joining those would invent words.

title: CORPUS: three sources duplicate content, inflating attestation counts
description: Attestation counts are the evidence a corpus-mined entry rests on, so a duplicated text overstates it. ia-poemo-de-utnoa-eo-1jun-2023.txt contains the whole poem twice — the second copy from about line 13100 is a degraded scan (num for nun, silneto for silueto, geornetrion) — so every count-2 candidate whose citations are both from that file is really one attestation. pg-61860 is a second edition of Marta, also held as wsdump-Orzeszko_Marta_1928_Zamenhof. pg-11511 and wsdump-Defoe_Robinsono_Kruso_1908_Krafft are both the 1908 Krafft Robinsono Kruso; an exact-line comparison found only 3.5% overlap, but the wsdump holds 100 of 128 pages and the two are broken into lines differently, so that test does not settle it — check by token shingles before acting.
close_reason:
Evaluated all three claims; two confirmed, one refuted, plus a fourth claim in the bead refuted. 8-gram token shingles settle it — pg-11511 and the Wikisource Robinsono Kruso are the same 1908 Krafft translation at 98.4% containment, pg-61860 and the Wikisource Marta the same text at 96.0%, against 0.0% for two unrelated books and 0.0% for the two volumes of Quo vadis. The exact-line test that appeared to refute this (3.5% of lines shared) was simply the wrong instrument: the same translation broken into lines differently shares almost no whole lines. Redundant copy of each pair quarantined, keeping the Gutenberg text as the more complete one — for Robinsono Kruso that trades 0.9 points of recognisability for 6% more of the book, which is the right way round.

REFUTED: ia-poemo-de-utnoa does not contain the poem twice. Split at its midpoint the halves share 4 8-grams out of 28000 tokens. Line 13100 begins ANEKSO 1, a critical essay quoting the poem — a 2048-token tail sharing 20.8% of its shingles with the body, so a few count-2 candidates there are one attestation plus one quotation. File stays.

ALSO REFUTED: the Wikisource Marta does not read t as l throughout — lempo, lasla and instruislino occur once each and akcepli and posluli not at all, against 84 correct occurrences of tempo. Not why it was moved.

Corpus 251 -> 249 sources; dictionary re-mined so the attestation counts reflect it: 27356 entries, corpus-mined 5126, 3626 attested in three or more independent sources.

title: CORPUS: five sources are OCR-corrupt in file-specific, repeatable ways
description: Round-5 reviewers traced most of the remaining artefact verdicts to five files, each with its own repeatable substitution table. ia-LaHeroojDeLaNovaTagiolaKronikoDeNabil (240k tokens, the largest source): u->tt/ii/nn (tittj, kiiijn, tinn), ŝ->e, ĝ->a, rm->nn (tunnento), plus dropped word spaces (lapersa, devasfari) — it supplied 314 of 400 derived and 164 of 240 unknown candidates in shard 1. wsdump-Orzeszko_Marta_1928_Zamenhof: pervasive t->l (lempo, lasla, akcepli, instruislino) — 55 of one reviewer's 69 artefact verdicts. wsdump-Voltaire_Tri_Verkoj_de_Volter_1956_Lanti: j->ĵ (24 tokens), m<->rn (ternpo, anirno), intruding i (ikiu, ised) — 73 of 120 candidates in one batch. ia-eowiki-Srana_lingvo, -Mezpersa_lingvo, -Parta_lingvo: every lowercase l scanned as i (iingvo, ia nederianda koionia) across every line. ia-eowiki-Rusa_lingvo and -Kopta_lingvo: Cyrillic and Coptic read as Latin lookalikes.
design: tools/repair_diacritics.py only does single-character substitutions against a closed target list, so it cannot reach u->tt or rm->nn. Either extend it with a per-source substitution table (the reviewers enumerated each one) or quarantine. Note the Nabil chronicle scores 92.1% recognisable and is the largest single source, so quarantine is expensive there; the three eowiki language articles are short and their l->i is total, so they are cheap to drop.
close_reason: Resolved by measurement rather than by the reported list. The 48 ia-eowiki articles are quarantined: mined with the current filters they yield 46.2 unknown candidates per 1000 tokens against 2.5 for three clean sources, for 0.6% of the corpus by tokens, and their top contributions are http, wikipedia, org, www, km. The three large sources named in this bead are deliberately NOT touched — the Nabil chronicle at 240802 tokens and 92.2% recognisable, Marta at 98.0%, Voltaire at 96.9%, together 390k tokens of otherwise good text where per-source substitution tables would be needed and the return is thin. Their scan errors reach reviewers as ocr-artifact verdicts, which is the correct handling. Also worth recording: the reviewers' claim that these files read every lowercase l as i was an overstatement — measured rates are 5.8%, 1.7% and 1.4% of tokens, and below about 0.5% the detector finds coincidences (sapiens->saplens, kaiser->kalser) rather than corruption.

title: DICT: re-merge ReVo from source to recover the variant forms
description: The comma-joined headwords are being repaired by truncation, which yields a valid headword for all 1466 but discards the second variant, because it cannot be decoded reliably from the joined string. The encoding is inconsistent: 'anarĥio,anarkio' holds two complete words, 'adultulo,ulino' holds a word and a differing tail whose shared prefix is unrecoverable, and 241 are mangled outright ('antigvo-barbudo,10okajbarbudooficialainformodeade,numero11'). Guessing produced 'adultuloulino' and 'aerarflugo', so it was not applied.
design: Re-run DICT/tools/merge_revo.py against a fresh ReVo XML checkout, where each variant is a separate drv element, and fix the joining there. The raw joined string is preserved on each repaired entry as revo_raw, so the affected entries can be found and replaced precisely.
notes:
Second defect from the same merge, found while repairing the first: ReVo multi-word heads lost their spaces, at every length. In the 18-21 character band, 94 of 97 headwords are affected — analitikageometrio (analytic geometry), gazetarakonferenco (press conference), bosniokajhercegovino (Bosnia and Herzegovina), nesole...sedankaŭ... — against 3 genuine single words (malproksimenpafanta, kontraŭrevoluciulo, paleoantropologiisto). So a length threshold is not available: it would delete real words and keep hundreds of malformed ones at shorter lengths.

Two automatic repairs were tried and rejected, both on measurement:
  * Segmenting into exact dictionary headwords marks 4014 entries, but it splits genuine single words just as readily — admiralo into 'ad mi ralo', adrenalino into 'ad rena lino', aeroplano into 'aero plano'. Unusable.
  * A length threshold of 22 characters was checked against the 18-21 band above and abandoned for the same reason.

The signal that does look real, for whoever does the re-merge: the affected heads are overwhelmingly adjective+noun, so the first piece ends in -a and the English gloss has exactly two words. That is a check to confirm a re-merge against, not a way to repair the current file.
close_reason:
Done from the source, not by rule. tools/fetch_revo_articles.py takes the ~1100 articles behind a damaged entry from reta-vortaro.de (the upstream GitHub repo is outside this session's scope) and tools/repair_revo_headwords.py renders each <kap> with <tld/> expanded inside <var> as well — which is exactly what the original merge failed to do. 810 of 1166 damaged entries recovered, 134 of them regaining a space: Aleksandro la Granda, Bosnujo kaj Hercegovino, artefarita intelekto, amina acido, stato de aferoj. 651 entries gained a variants field. Zero duplicate headwords, zero commas.

Three separate defects of the one merge are now on record: the comma-joined variant pairs, the flattened spaces in multi-word heads, and a wrong root field where the merge took the last component of a compound (aerarmeo carries root 'arme' where ReVo files it under 'aer') — that third one was found only because the repair verifies an article's own <rad> before using it, a guard added after noticing the fetcher caches a fallback article under the name originally asked for.

356 entries not recovered and left with their truncated headword plus revo_raw: 208 whose article could not be fetched (73 are simply not retrievable under any name tried) and 197 whose recorded root points at the wrong article. Their headwords are already valid words; what they lack is the variant. Chasing them means guessing article names from the word and costs roughly 1500 more requests against a volunteer-run server for 350 variants, which is not worth it.

title: Review interface: no verdict for solid numerals or authorial coinages
description: Reviewers on shards 3, 4, 6 and 8 all reported candidates the closed verdict set cannot express. Solid-written compound numerals (okdekkvin, dudeksepa, tridekses, dekkvarulo) are regular formations from an infinite set, so calling them 'lemma' would put arbitrary numbers in the dictionary and calling them 'inflection' is untrue. Author-invented words glossed in their own source (six from Poemo de Utnoa, marked '(g)' in its glossary at line 12630; three Burroughs beast names; Rossetti's deliberate accent-parody spellings, which one reviewer filed as ocr-artifact for want of anywhere better) are attested and real but belong to one text. Both were being forced into the wrong bucket or left uncertain.
design: Add 'numeral' and 'nonce' to the closed set in review_shard.py. Neither promotes — promote_lemmas takes only 'lemma' — so they record the judgement without growing the dictionary, and the count of each becomes visible in the reduce summary.
close_reason: Added 'numeral' and 'nonce' to the closed verdict set in review_shard.py, with the reasoning documented in the docstring reviewers read first. Neither promotes, so they record a judgement without growing the dictionary. In use from round 5.

title: RAW: wsdump-Vallienne_Ĉu_li_1908 has mid-word text dropouts
description: The shard 6 reviewer found 12 of its 19 fragment verdicts came from this one file: text is missing mid-word, leaving head and tail halves as candidates — tino, rimentado (eksperimentadoj), gnaĵo (desegnaĵoj), ciza (precizan), ĉeco (feliĉecon), glo (pinglojn), trante (montrante), stre (dekstren), nas (bezonas), kuteble (nediskuteble), ciĝo, neco. Line 8758 jumps from 'kiu montris' to 'tino ĉiujn amrilatojn'. Likely a page or section lost during extraction rather than a scan defect; re-extract and compare page count against the index.
close_reason: Already fixed by the vdk/vdf repair in round 4, and the diagnosis in this bead was wrong about the cause. The orphan halves were not text dropouts: eo.wikisource marks a word split across a page break with {{vdk|head|tail}} at the foot of one page and {{vdf|head|tail}} at the head of the next, and the resolver returned only the tail from both. All 12 forms the reviewer named are now 0 occurrences (tino, rimentado, gnaĵo, ciza, trante, kuteble; ĉeco and stre were grep artefacts matching inside feliĉeco and dekstre). What does remain is 165 page-gap splice points across the qualifying books, where the quality gate drops an unproofread page between two kept ones — Robinsono Kruso has 34, most books 1-3. Those lose whole sentences, not word halves, and each file's header records the count ('448 proofread pages of 458 scanned'), so the loss is visible rather than silent.

title: Apostrophes in the tokenizer manufacture pseudo-lemmas
description: TOKEN accepts the apostrophe, so three distinct constructions arrive as vocabulary. Elided article in verse (pg-8224): l'homaro, l'aero, l'espero, l'afero, l'ordonanto, l'vivo, l'infano, l'aĥajo — nine in one shard. Zamenhof's early morpheme-separated spelling (pg-75983, pg-8224): inter'naci'e, sci'i, frat'in'o. Eye-dialect elision (pg-17665, pg-48900, Rossetti): h'm, s'prizo, n'nio, s'pozi, kam'rado, 'strordinare. Reported independently by the shard 4, 5 and 6 reviewers; 13 of 21 fragments in shard 5 were this.
design: In the miner, split a token on internal apostrophes and drop a leading l' before analysis. The trailing apostrophe (hord' for hordo) is already handled by citation_form and must stay.
close_reason: mine_lemmas.normalise_token now resolves the three constructions separately: the elided article is dropped (l'homaro -> homaro), Zamenhof's morpheme-separated spelling is joined when the result is recognisable (inter'naci'e -> internacie, frat'in'o -> fratino), and eye-dialect elision is rejected outright (h'm, n'nio, 'strordinare). dank' al is kept as written, since the apostrophe there elides an ending in a fixed expression.

title: CORPUS: pg-60429 arrived double-encoded and its diacritics were lost
description: RAW/pg-60429.txt (Goethe, Hermano kaj Doroteo, 1922) is valid UTF-8 but doubly mojibaked: 'ĝ' (C4 9D) arrives as 'Ã\\x84Â\\x9d'. The damage was invisible because the file simply appeared to have zero diacritics, which then made the h-system gate misfire on its English licence text and convert taghelaj to 'taĝelaj'.
design: Repair before slicing: round-trip each run of high Latin-1 characters through latin-1/utf-8 until it stops changing, and keep the result only where it decodes. A genuinely Latin-1 run (Achtélik) fails to decode and is left alone. Recovers 2504 diacritics; the file scores 97.7% recognisable afterwards, among the cleanest in the corpus.
close_reason: Fixed in tools/normalize_corpus.py: repair_mojibake runs before slicing. 2504 diacritics recovered; pg-60429 now scores 97.7% recognisable and 18773 tokens of Goethe enter the corpus as Esperanto instead of replacement characters. Only one RAW source is affected; the detector is general and gated at 20 runs.

title: CORPUS: h-system gate misses foreign-language textbooks
description: pg-24575 (a Czech-language Esperanto textbook) writes its Esperanto in the h-system but also quotes diacritic spellings, so the diacritic ratio is 0.15 and is_hsystem's 0.05 threshold rejects the file. Result: regho, ghi, chiuj, ech reach the review queue as vocabulary. Same shape in ia-key_to_the_ekzercaro (0.11) and ia-traduction_de_lekzercaro (0.17).
design: Raise HSYS_MAX_DIACRITIC_RATIO from 0.05 to 0.20. Only four RAW files sit in the 0.05-0.60 band, and real diacritic prose has diacritics outnumbering digraph hits by ~50x, so the threshold is not delicate. The Universala vortaro at 0.31 stays unconverted, correctly: it lists both spellings.
close_reason: Replaced the diacritic-ratio proxy with a measured gate (conversion_is_sound): convert only if the substitution turns more distinct spellings into Esperanto words than it breaks. Fixes pg-24575 (now converted, 63.8%->70.0% recognisable), keeps the English/French Ekzercaro translations unconverted, and newly rejects pg-60429, whose 104 'digraphs' were all in the English licence.

title: RAW: triage the 57 archive.org sources by text quality
description: PR #8 added 57 ia-* sources. Scored with tools/score_esperanto_text.py (recognisable-token rate against DICT/entries.jsonl, plus single-character-token rate as an OCR tell): 14 are usable (>=80% recognisable, <5% singles — best is ia-LaHeroojDeLaNovaTago at 240802 tokens and 90.6%, then ia-poemo-de-utnoa at 89.5% and the eowiki PDFs at 80-85%), 18 are marginal (65-80%), and 23 are poor (<65% or >=10% single-char tokens). Real Esperanto scores 90%+ on this metric. The worst are ia-Pichismo (27.4%, 108% singles — 73 tokens of noise) and ia-KvarvoajKantojPorEsperantistoj (56.1%, 36.9% singles). Three of the 'poor' ones are not corrupt but simply not Esperanto — key_to_the_ekzercaro (English), traduction_de_lekzercaro (French) and the Downes textbook — and are now in the mining exclusion list rather than treated as bad text. Recommend dropping or quarantining the 23 poor ones before the next mining round, since the low-frequency band is exactly where OCR noise becomes fake lemmas.
acceptance_criteria: Each of the 23 poor sources is kept with a documented reason or moved out of RAW/; the marginal 18 have a decision recorded.
notes: Triaged all 57. Scoring ranks but does not classify — each low scorer was read before any decision. QUARANTINED 3 that are genuinely unusable: the Quran translation (82121 tokens of broken machine translation, 'This scripture est infallible; beacon por des righteous'), KvarvoajKantoj (corrupt scan, largely English advertising) and Pichismo (73 words of scanner noise). KEPT the rest, because the metric was wrong about them: the 41 eowiki language articles are real Esperanto whose low scores come from alphabet tables (a run of single letters reads as 46% single-char tokens) and from quoting the language each describes; ia-dlibra is a genuine bilingual Esperanto-German periodical at 70.6% Esperanto. The three English/French texts stay in RAW/ and are excluded from mining, as the other English-language grammars already are. RAW/QUALITY.tsv records every source's score.
close_reason: Triaged: 3 quarantined, 3 excluded from mining, the rest kept with the evidence recorded in RAW/QUALITY.tsv.

title: DICT: 8 duplicate headwords after the ReVo merge
description: DICT/entries.jsonl contains 8 words twice, each once from Fundamento/UV-1905 and once from a ReVo layer: dio, julia, kristo, mario, marto, mesio, pasko, pentekosto — the capitalised-in-source religious and calendar terms. A duplicate key makes lookup ambiguous and inflates the entry count. Introduced by the ReVo merge in PR #6, not by the corpus-mined or O'Connor layers, both of which skip words already held. Fixing needs a decision on which layer wins for a word present in both: the Fundamento gloss is authoritative for the 1905 core, but ReVo's is likely fuller. Left for whoever owns the ReVo merge semantics rather than resolved unilaterally.
acceptance_criteria: Zero duplicate word keys in DICT/entries.jsonl, with the precedence rule recorded in DICT/README.md.
close_reason: Fixed in the same pass. The eight were case variants from two sources, not a judgement call: the Fundamento capitalises a proper noun and ReVo does not. Each pair is merged keeping the Fundamento spelling, and a sense the losing entry had is carried across rather than dropped — Dio is now 'God; god' and Pasko 'Easter; Passover'. Seven more pairs of the same shape turned up once truncation exposed them (Aprilo/aprilo,o and the other month names), so 15 in total. Duplicate headwords in entries.jsonl: 0.

title: DICT: review 11 period-dated English glosses inherited from O'Connor 1906
description: The O'Connor layer takes its English glosses verbatim from a 1906 dictionary, so a handful carry period usage that a present-day artefact should not repeat unmarked: nigrulo 'negro', idolano 'heathen', lunatikulo 'lunatic', malspritulo 'imbecile', kriplulo/kripligi 'cripple', idiotulo 'idiot', muta 'dumb', sovaĝa 'savage', orienta 'oriental', pantomimo 'dumb show'. Full list from: grep the oconnor-1906 entries for the period-term pattern in the tool's own scan. This is a small, bounded set of 11 out of 5935. Three defensible options: (a) keep O'Connor's wording as a historical record, since the source tag already marks provenance; (b) add a modern gloss alongside and keep the original in a dated_gloss field; (c) replace outright. I did not decide this unilaterally — the entries are shipped as the source has them, and the source tag makes their provenance explicit.
acceptance_criteria: A decision recorded in DICT/README.md and applied to the 11 entries.
close_reason: Middle option, as chosen: gloss_en carries a present-day gloss and the 1906 wording is preserved verbatim in a new dated_gloss field, so nothing is deleted and the provenance stays legible. Eight entries, not eleven — three of the bead's list (fawn-coloured, poppy-coloured, tri-coloured) were matched only by a loose pattern and are innocuous. Applied by tools/modernise_glosses.py, which is idempotent and must be re-run after a rebuild.

title: DICT: settle the lemma/inflection boundary for affix derivations
description: The eight shard reviewers disagreed on 37 lemmas, and nearly all of them are one policy question the brief under-specified: when is a productive affix derivation a dictionary headword rather than an inflection? Concretely they split on reĝino (471), reĝidino (215), duono (248), kvarono (95), treege (188), senĉese (171), speciale (167), absolute (276). One reviewer filed -in-/-on-/-eg- derivations and adverbs-of-adjectives as inflections of a 1905 root; another filed them as lexicalised headwords. Both are defensible and both were applied consistently within their own shard, so the split is a missing convention, not reviewer error. Everyone agreed on the easy ends: transparent two-root compounds (lernolibro, skribtablo) are lemmas, and finite verb forms (eniris, enhavas) are inflections. Decide the rule, record it in DICT/README.md, and re-run the review layer against it.
acceptance_criteria: A written rule in DICT/README.md, and the disputed entries in DICT/candidates.jsonl reconciled to match it.
close_reason: Settled: productive derivations earn entries and are surfaced for review as their own lemmas; the underlying peel_affixes bug that caused most of the disagreement is fixed.

title: RAW: expand the corpus with more public-domain Esperanto sources
description: RAW/ holds 89 texts (10 Project Gutenberg, 79 Vikifontaro). Find and add further freely-licensed Esperanto sources, following the established conventions: pg-<id>.txt / wsrc-<Page_title>.txt naming, sha256 exact-copy dedup against what is already present, and one PROVENANCE.md line per source recording title, author, hash, licence and URL. Prefer original Esperanto prose and Zamenhof-era material over more translations, since the DICT and GRAMMAR passes need attested native usage.
notes: Done in three parts. (1) Project Gutenberg: 30 curated public-domain texts added via tools/fetch_raw_gutenberg.py, out of the 145 Esperanto titles in its catalogue; skipped the 27 bilingual Esperantist issues and the translations of foreign classics. (2) archive.org: evaluated and rejected — see the corpus-sources memory; 511/820 are eowiki PDF dumps and 264/300 non-Wikipedia items are Google scans whose OCR invents lemmas (74.8% known-word rate, 7% single-char tokens, vs 86-88%/1% for clean text). tools/score_esperanto_text.py is the gate built for that judgement and is reusable. (3) Vikifontaro: 13 whole books added via tools/fetch_raw_vikifontaro.py from the XML dump, taking only human-proofread pages (ProofreadPage quality >= 3) from books published <= 1929. RAW/ is now 132 sources / 16 MB / 264355 normalized body lines, up from 89 / 3.1 MB / 57709.
close_reason: 43 sources added (30 Gutenberg, 13 Vikifontaro whole books); archive.org evaluated and rejected with the finding recorded.

title: GRAMMAR: write the rule sections with corpus citations
description: Expand each outline section into prose, and back every claim with a citation from the normalized corpus rather than from memory. Flag any rule where corpus usage diverges from the stated rule.
notes: Rewrote GRAMMAR/grammar.md from 95 to 228 lines, every checkable claim cited against CORPUS/ as *quote* — source:line or by frequency count, using the new tools/find_examples.py. Citations are machine-verifiable and were verified: 9/9 quotations appear at the line given. Corrected three errors the corpus exposed: the correlative table had the -al (reason) and -el (manner) rows swapped, contradicted by 'Kial vi malĝojas' vs 'kiel arbo'; the -es possessive row was missing entirely from a table described as 45 words; and rule 12 claimed double negatives are normal, where the corpus shows 5965 neni- lines against 10 with ne+neni-. Also fixed a nonsense elision example (bel' ulo). Added §6 recording where period usage diverges: -ujo beats -io 172:1 for Francujo, and the h-system is documented alongside the x-system since one source uses it.
close_reason: Guide rewritten with verified corpus citations; three substantive errors corrected and divergences documented.

title: DICT: mine lemmas and citations from the literary corpus
description: Harvest attested word forms from the Zamenhof/Andersen translations and the other literary pg-* sources, lemmatize by stripping regular Esperanto endings, and attach real citations to entries. Feeds coverage numbers and catches words the O'Connor pass misses.
design: Map-reduce over the corpus. MAP: tools/mine_lemmas.py --shard I/N reads only its assigned CORPUS/ files (packed greedily by size, since the corpus is lopsided) and writes only DICT/shards/shard-I-of-N.jsonl, so shards run concurrently with no coordination. REVIEW: tools/review_shard.py gives each reviewer --list/--apply/--status over one shard; shard files are ~4MB so they are never read or hand-edited directly, and the closed verdict set is validated on apply. REDUCE: tools/reconcile_lemmas.py merges shards, summing counts, preferring citation breadth across sources over repetition within one, taking the strictest kind any shard assigned, and recording verdict disagreements as conflicts rather than silently resolving them. Shared morphology lives in tools/esperanto.py, used by the miner and the scorer.
notes: Ran the pipeline with 8 parallel reviewers over the 131-source corpus. 1087 verdicts assigned: 518 accepted as lemmas (445 attested in 3+ independent sources), 301 proper nouns, 122 inflections, 52 foreign, 9 fragments, 1 OCR artefact. Reviewers found four defects that were mine, not the corpus's, all now fixed: citation_form stripped a final -n as accusative and invented stems from foreign names (Hutton→hutto, London→londo, Einstein→einstei), reported independently by four shards; the elided article l' was mined 2884 times; Roman numerals and subject-label abbreviations (zool, ĥem, med) ranked in the top 20; and normalize_corpus.py handled x-system but not h-system, so pg-32035 (3961 digraphs, zero diacritics) produced ~30 false candidates per shard. Also repaired 28 Cyrillic homoglyph tokens in three Dua Libro files, found by shard 7 and verified independently. After the fixes: distinct lemmas 19812→17959, unknown 13322→9004 (-32%), with 2995 now correctly classified as names.
close_reason: Pipeline built, run, and verified; 518 lemmas accepted with glosses and citations. Long tail and the lemma/inflection policy question tracked separately.

title: normalize_corpus leaves Project Gutenberg's 'Edition N, (date)' line in CORPUS body text
description:
Several CORPUS files begin with a surviving PG front-matter line, e.g. CORPUS/pg-21194.txt:5 'Edition 1, (April 20, 2007)' and CORPUS/pg-25386.txt:8 'Edition 1, (May 8, 2008)'. It is the digitisation date, not anything about the text, and it is the earliest year in the file, so it feeds the intext dating rule directly.

date_sources.py now strikes years matching the RAW/ header's Release date / Most recently updated as a guard, which is a patch on the output. Per 'fix the extractor, not the text' the line should be stripped in normalize_corpus.py instead. Measure first: how many CORPUS files carry it, and whether any currently-dated source got its year from one.

title: ANALYSIS: 14 translator names unresolved in Wikidata, 11 sources still undated
description:
tools/date_by_translator.py resolves 34 of 48 translator names. The 14 that fail leave 11 sources undated that carry a usable in-text year: Adolf Krafft (1908), Gary Mickle (2001), J. W. Eggleton, Ivan H. Krestanoff (1922), E. Neumark (1893), Benedict Papot (1909), G. Vaillant (1906), Venancio Da Silva (1912), Alexander Pride (1907), A. Muller (1912), Alexandra Mexin (1923).

Four are initials-only (A. Muller, E. Neumark, G. Vaillant, D. H. Lambert-style) and wbsearchentities cannot match them; five got no Wikidata hit at all. Enciklopedio de Esperanto (1933) and the Vikipedio category Esperantistoj both cover several of these people and are the obvious next place to look. Do NOT date them from the in-text year without an independent lifespan: that is the gate esp-e0q deliberately did not relax.

title: DICT: re-merge ReVo to repair the whitespace-squashed headwords
description: merge_revo.py squashes whitespace out of every headword, so ReVo's multi-word terms arrive welded: 'Aleksandro la Granda' as 'aleksandrolagranda', 'propozicia kalkulo' as 'propoziciakalkulo', and one candidate as 'turnigxantapontoturneblaopiv1' — two variants and a source marker run into one string. tools/repair_revo_headwords.py restored the spaces on entries that made it in, but 118 heads in the 970-article cache alone are still absent in any form and cannot be added safely from the merge's output, because a squashed compound cannot be told from a real one by looking at it. Needs the full revo-fonto source and a merge that preserves the <kap> whitespace.
acceptance_criteria: merge_revo.py preserves headword whitespace; a re-merge adds the multi-word terms currently missing; tools/restore_revo_gaps.py reports zero in its 'not a single word' bucket.

title: ANALYSIS: separate original Esperanto from translated Esperanto, and literary from movement prose
description: Two confounds named in ANALYSIS/diachronic.md and not yet controlled. (1) A translation's register follows its source text and the corpus is majority translation. (2) Eight of the ten texts that use -io are movement or reference prose (Historio de Esperanto, Dokumentoj de Esperanto, Kabe's Vortaro, Lanti's Naciismo), so register is confounded with date the same way author was. Both need a per-source flag in RAW/PROVENANCE.md or DATES.tsv before any further diachronic claim.
acceptance_criteria: Each dated source carries original/translated and literary/movement flags; tools/diachronic.py can hold either out.

title: Mining: the Fundamento Ekzercaro's gloss columns are mined as Esperanto
description: wsrc-Fundamento_de_Esperanto_Ekzercaro.txt prints its French, English, German, Polish and Russian translations beside the Esperanto, and 18 of one reviewer's 33 foreign verdicts came from it: earth, ziemia, dobry, czysty, homme, mourir, scheere, gold, vremja. Its sibling files (Universala_vortaro, Grammar) are already in MULTILINGUAL and excluded; the Ekzercaro is not, because unlike them it is also a core Esperanto text worth mining. The per-line filter does not catch it, so the gloss words must share lines with the Esperanto — confirm that before choosing between excluding the file and teaching the filter to split the line.
close_reason: Fixed without excluding the file, which would have cost a core Esperanto text. mine_lemmas.foreign_columns is a fourth scale of language filter beside file, line and span. Deciding it needed a stricter test than the others: pipes alone are wrong (pg-42028 tables Esperanto vocabulary in columns, pg-51690 marks verse scansion) and ordinary recognisability is wrong too, because the morphology builds 'father' and reads 'Vater' as the root vat-. A later column counts as Esperanto only if a token, or a token minus one ending, is a root or headword the dictionary lists. The French gloss in the kept first column goes too, since 'patro père' otherwise leaks père, terre, homme and mourir.

title: citation_form reduces Latin binomials as if they were Esperanto verbs
description: Kabe's Vortaro prints botanical and zoological binomials inside Esperanto lines — '(Musca domestica)' — and citation_form strips the Latin -us/-is as an Esperanto tense ending, so domesticus files as 'domestici', communis as 'communi', and cristatus, aureus, matutinus, maximus likewise. Six reached the shard 7 reviewer disguised as verbs. Latin is the one language the per-line filter cannot catch, because the binomial sits inside an otherwise Esperanto sentence.
close_reason: Fixed at the source rather than in citation_form: mine_lemmas.foreign_spans now skips a parenthesis of two to four tokens in which nothing is recognisable Esperanto, so the binomial never reaches citation_form to be mis-analysed. The parenthesis pattern alone cannot decide it — the same shape holds Esperanto stage directions, (Vilhelmo silentas), (Volas iri) — but recognisability inside the span can, and one recognisable word keeps the whole span. Measured over the mined corpus: 517 spans, 730 distinct tokens, comprising the Latin binomials (Abies pectinata, Ascaris lumbricoides, Buphagus africanus), translator credits (translated by Clarence Bicknell), currency notes and citation shorthand (ibid, pp, Oxon). Takes effect at the next re-mine.

title: RAW: Quo vadis I scan drops a leading letter in ~113 places
description: wsdump-Sienkiewikz_Quo_vadis_1934_Zamenhof_I.txt contains 'ezaro' as a standalone word 113 times where the text means 'cezaro' (Caesar), alongside 132 correct spellings — the leading c is lost. Found by a shard-7 reviewer and verified independently. The reviewer marked it ocr-artifact so it cannot reach the dictionary, but the corpus text itself is still wrong and any citation drawn from those lines will read oddly. Same file also shows stray 'la la' sequences where a noun was dropped. Options: a per-source correction table in tools/normalize_corpus.py (the homoglyph repair is the precedent), or leave it and rely on the artifact verdict.
acceptance_criteria: Either the corrections are applied and the count of standalone 'ezaro' is zero, or the bead is closed recording that the artifact verdict is sufficient.
close_reason: Root cause found and fixed upstream, not patched: the wikitext reads {{SIC|c|C}}ezaro 132 times — Wikisource editors marking that the book prints a lowercase initial — and our template resolver filtered both arguments away as alignment codes. Verified against the dump's own wikitext. After re-extraction standalone 'ezaro' is 0. The 'la la' sequences in the same file had a second cause, the unrecognised {{Lingvo|la|frigidarium}}, also fixed: 105 down to 3.

title: DICT: review the long tail of mined candidates
description: The eight reviewers judged the top 120-360 candidates per shard by frequency, 1087 verdicts in total. 16955 candidates remain unreviewed, almost all at count 2-9. Value drops sharply with frequency, and the remaining band is where OCR artefacts concentrate (reviewers found almost none in the high-frequency band because the clean digital sources dominate it). The mechanism is in place and re-runnable: raise the --top cap in tools/review_shard.py --list and re-run the review layer. tools/mine_lemmas.py --ledger restores existing verdicts, so re-mining costs nothing. Two known biases to correct for: frequency ranking within one shard over-weights whichever book that shard drew (shard 5's top entries are one novel's cast list), and pg-24292 is a modern translation whose vocabulary is anachronistic for a 1905-1922 layer.
notes: Round 2 complete: eight agents judged ~4,400 further candidates (300+ unknown and 200+ derived per shard). Verdicts now 2,980 in the ledger; 2,216 promoted to the dictionary, which stands at 5,127 entries. Reviewers found five more defects in the tooling, all fixed: a final -n stripped as accusative from names and directional adverbs (martin, malsupren, dekkvin); finite verb forms not collapsed, so eliris/eliras/eliros were three candidates rather than one eliri; imperatives and apostrophe elisions (eliru, hord') filed as bare stems; pg-32035 still carrying ~200 unconverted bare-u spellings of ŭ; and the Fundamento index page feeding German and Polish gloss-column words into the queue.
close_reason: Round 2 done; dictionary at 5127 entries. Remaining tail tracked by the same re-runnable mechanism.

title: RAW: revisit Vikifontaro books blocked by the 1929 cutoff or unproofread OCR
description: tools/fetch_raw_vikifontaro.py --list shows the near-misses. Two groups worth revisiting. (a) Copyright cutoff: Quo vadis? I+II (1934, Zamenhof, 537 proofread pages), Verkoj de FeZ (1935, 261), Kredu min Sinjorino! (1950, 258), Enciklopedio de Esperanto (1933, 112), Tri Verkoj de Volter (1956, 308). All are proofread and would be valuable; whether they can be included depends on the jurisdiction and on Wikisource's own licence claim, which is a human call. (b) Unproofread: La Sankta Biblio 1927 is 995 pages but 974 sit at quality level 1 (raw OCR), so it is excluded by the quality gate — it would need proofreading upstream, or a different edition. Zamenhof's Bible translation is a major gap in the corpus.
acceptance_criteria: Either the post-1929 books are cleared for inclusion and fetched, or the bead is closed recording why they cannot be.
close_reason: Resolved: corpus now uses the union of the source-country (life+70, Wikidata-verified) and US (95-year) terms; 10 further books added.

title: Cross-link DICT entries to GRAMMAR sections
description: Once both artifacts exist, link affix and correlative entries in DICT/ to the GRAMMAR/ sections that explain them, so the dictionary is navigable alongside the guide.
close_reason: tools/link_grammar.py adds a 'grammar' field to the 181 entries a gloss cannot serve alone: 45 correlatives, 48 affixes and endings, 88 articles, pronouns, prepositions, conjunctions, particles and numerals. Mapping is by part of speech and by the correlative pattern, never by a hand-written word list, so it stays correct as the dictionary grows, and load_sections exits rather than writing if a heading it targets has moved.

title: DICT: extract headwords from O'Connor dictionary (pg-16967)
description: Supplementary source now that DICT/entries.jsonl is seeded from the Fundamento UV-1905 (PR #5, 2911 entries). pg-16967 (O'Connor English-Esperanto) adds the English→Esperanto lookup direction and post-1905 vocabulary the UV core does not carry, so this is enrichment layered onto the existing schema, not a rebuild. Parse from CORPUS/pg-16967.txt (already de-boilerplated; note it was deliberately NOT x-system converted, since its English side contains words like 'auxiliary' and 'flux'). Record what was dropped.
design: Scoped by measurement rather than guesswork. pg-16967 parses cleanly with one regex ('English = esperanto.' per line, parentheticals carrying sense): 13940 pairs, 9244 distinct Esperanto words, of which 6844 are absent from the current 3429-entry dictionary. Splitting those by our own morphology: 4481 are regular derivations of roots we already hold (malsekigi, pendigi, malĝojo) and 2363 rest on a root we do not (kaŭĉuko, galvanismo, septimo). So the genuinely new lexical material is roughly 2363 roots, not 6844 words — and whether the other 4481 deserve entries is precisely the lemma/inflection boundary question in esp-5fe. Two further gains independent of that: the English->Esperanto direction, which the dictionary currently cannot serve at all, and sense disambiguation (1084 Esperanto words carry 3+ English headwords, plus O'Connor's parenthetical senses like 'Clean (boots, etc.) = senkotigi').
close_reason: O'Connor parsed and merged: 5935 new entries, a 12497-headword English index, and 56 affix segmentation examples.
